places.name: Intramuros
places.line: Manila's old walled Spanish city, with stone churches, forts and cobbled lanes.
places.about: Inside thick 16th century walls sit Fort Santiago, the San Agustin Church (a World Heritage site) and rebuilt colonial houses. It is the calmest part of central Manila and easy to explore on foot, by bike or by horse cart.
tips: Rent a bamboo bike or join a walking tour from the Intramuros Visitors Center at Fort Santiago.
Walk the top of the walls at sunset; most stretches are free and breezy.
Horse cart (kalesa) drivers ask high prices: agree the route and total before you get in.

fees.what: Fort Santiago (students, seniors, under 18 with ID)

places.timeOfDay: Start at Fort Santiago when it opens at 8 am, rest indoors in museums over midday, then walk the walls from 4:30 pm for sunset.

popular.name: San Agustin Church

places.name: Binondo food crawl
places.line: The world's oldest Chinatown, best eaten one dumpling at a time.
places.about: Binondo was founded in 1594 for Chinese traders and is still a busy maze of shops, temples and tiny eateries. Come hungry and graze along Ongpin Street and the narrow lanes around it.
tips: Go on a weekday morning or at lunch; many places close by 8 pm.
Bring small notes and coins: most stalls are cash only.
Keep phones and wallets in front pockets in the crowded lanes.
places.timeOfDay: Arrive about 10 am, eat through lunch, and finish with coffee before the afternoon heat and traffic build.

popular.name: Binondo Church

popular.name: Ongpin Street

crowd.busiest: Chinese New Year week, when lion dances fill the streets, and weekend lunchtimes.
crowd.note: Streets flood in typhoon rain; check the weather from July to October.

places.name: Poblacion, Makati nightlife
places.line: Manila's liveliest bar district, packed into a few old streets.
places.about: Poblacion is the old heart of Makati, now full of rooftop bars, craft beer, food halls and tiny clubs. It gets going late and stays busy until the early hours, with a mixed local and foreign crowd.
tips: Book a Grab car home; queues for rides build after midnight.
Carry ID: some bars and clubs check it at the door.
Watch your drink and belongings in the busiest bars on weekends.

fees.what: Some clubs, weekend cover charge with a drink

places.timeOfDay: Have dinner from 8 pm, bar hop from 10 pm, and expect clubs to peak between midnight and 3 am.

places.name: Banaue Rice Terraces
places.line: Mountain walls of rice fields carved by hand over centuries.
places.about: The Ifugao people built these stone and mud terraces up steep valleys around Banaue, and many families still farm them. The views from the road viewpoints are grand; the walks between villages are better.
tips: Hire a registered local guide at the tourism office for village walks; trails are slippery.
Take a jacket: nights in the mountains are cool, especially from December to February.
Ask before photographing people in traditional dress; some expect a small tip.
places.best: Mar to May (planting is green), Jun to Jul (gold before harvest)

places.timeOfDay: Catch the main viewpoint early, about 6 to 8 am, before mist and clouds roll in, then walk in the cooler morning.

places.name: Batad
places.line: A village sitting in a bowl of rice terraces, reached only on foot.
places.about: Batad's amphitheatre of terraces is the most striking in Ifugao and part of the World Heritage listing. There are no cars in the village: you walk down from the saddle, stay in simple lodges and hike to Tappiya Falls.
tips: Leave big bags in Banaue; the walk in is steep stone steps.
Hire a guide in the village for Tappiya Falls and the terrace paths.
Bring cash: there is no ATM and power can be patchy.
places.best: Mar to May, Jun to Jul

fees.what: Tricycle or jeep from Banaue to the saddle, per vehicle

places.timeOfDay: Walk in by mid morning, see the terraces in afternoon light, then hike to the falls early the next day before the heat.

places.name: Sagada
places.line: A cool pine forest town with caves and coffins hung on cliffs.
places.about: Sagada sits high in the Cordillera, with misty mornings, caves to scramble through and the old custom of hanging coffins on limestone walls. It is laid back, with good coffee and walking in every direction.
tips: Register at the tourism office on arrival; you get a receipt to show at sites.
Caves and Echo Valley need an accredited guide, arranged at the guides' office.
Respect the burial sites: do not touch the coffins and keep voices low.
places.timeOfDay: Wake by 4:30 am for the Kiltepan sunrise over the sea of clouds, then do caves late morning when it warms up.

places.name: Vigan heritage town
places.line: Cobbled Spanish colonial streets that look as they did 200 years ago.
places.about: Vigan is the best kept Spanish era town in Asia and a World Heritage site. Stone and wood mansions line Calle Crisologo, horse carts clatter past, and the food is some of the best in the north.
tips: Walk Calle Crisologo after dark when the lamps are lit and it is cooler.
Kalesa drivers offer town tours; agree the price per hour first.
Try the empanada and longganisa: Vigan's own versions are famous.

places.timeOfDay: Walk early morning for empty streets and photos, rest at midday, and come back at dusk for the lights and the Plaza Salcedo fountain show.

places.name: Baguio
places.line: The pine covered summer capital, cool, hilly and arty.
places.about: Baguio sits at about 1,500 metres and is where lowlanders escape the heat. It is a busy city with heavy traffic, but has parks, markets, strawberry farms and a lively art and café scene.
tips: Avoid driving up on Friday evenings and long weekends; traffic is terrible.
Buy fresh vegetables, strawberries and peanut brittle at the public market.
Bring a jacket: evenings can drop to 12 to 15 °C from December to February.
places.timeOfDay: Mornings are clearest and cool; mist and rain often roll in by mid afternoon, especially from June to October.

places.name: San Juan, La Union surf town
places.line: A friendly surf town and the north's favourite beach break.
places.about: San Juan's Urbiztondo beach has gentle waves for beginners, a strip of cafés and hostels, and a young, relaxed crowd. It is an easy bus ride from Manila and a stop on the way to Vigan or Baguio.
tips: Surf season is roughly October to March; summer waves are small but fine for first lessons.
Book a lesson with an accredited instructor; ask what the rate includes.
Watch the sunset from the beach: the sky over the sea is the show here.

places.timeOfDay: Surf early morning when wind is light, rest at midday, and be on the beach for sunset from about 5:30 pm.

places.name: Taal Volcano from Tagaytay
places.line: A volcano inside a lake, seen from a cool ridge above it.
places.about: Tagaytay's ridge looks down on Taal Lake and the small volcano island in the middle. The island is a permanent danger zone and closed to visitors, so this is a place for views, cool air and long lunches of bulalo.
tips: Do not book trips onto Volcano Island: entry is banned and the crater is off limits.
Check the PHIVOLCS alert level before you go; ash or vog can bring advice to wear a mask.
Avoid weekends if you can: the ridge road jams with day trippers from Manila.
places.timeOfDay: Arrive by 8 to 9 am for the clearest views before cloud and haze build after midday.

places.name: Puerto Galera
places.line: Bays, reefs and beaches a few hours from Manila.
places.about: Puerto Galera on Mindoro mixes a party beach (White Beach), a dive hub (Sabang) and calm coves in a sheltered bay. The reefs of the Verde Island Passage are some of the richest in the world for fish and coral.
tips: Take a bus to Batangas port, then a fast boat; aim to cross before early afternoon when seas get choppy.
Pick your beach: White Beach for nightlife, Sabang for diving, Small La Laguna for quiet.
Bring cash for the town's environmental fee and the Batangas terminal fee.

places.name: Mayon Volcano
places.line: A near perfect cone of a volcano, active and restless.
places.about: Mayon rises over Albay in a classic cone shape and is one of the most active volcanoes in the country. It erupted through the first half of 2026 and is watched closely, so this is a place to view it from a safe distance, not to climb.
tips: Check the PHIVOLCS alert level before going; the 6 km zone around the summit is closed.
Lahars can follow heavy rain on the old lava slopes; avoid river channels after storms.
Clouds hide the top most afternoons; mornings give the best chance of a clear cone.

places.name: Donsol whale sharks
places.line: Swim with wild whale sharks in their own feeding grounds.
places.about: From about December to May, whale sharks (butanding) feed in the plankton rich waters off Donsol. Trips here are run by the town with spotters and trained guides, and there is no feeding, so sightings are never promised.
tips: Register at the Butanding Interaction Center the day you arrive; the fee lasts five days.
Follow the rules: no touching, no flash, and stay about 3 metres away.
Book early for February to April, the peak months.

places.timeOfDay: Boats go out from 7:30 am; go on the first trips when the sea is calmest and spotters see the sharks best.

places.name: El Nido and Bacuit Bay
places.line: Limestone islands, hidden lagoons and some of the clearest water in Asia.
places.about: El Nido town sits on Bacuit Bay, which is dotted with sheer limestone islands. Boat tours (named A to D) visit lagoons, coves and beaches; the town itself is busy and the bay is the reason to come.
tips: Pay the Eco-Tourism Development Fee once and keep the tag: it covers 10 days.
Lagoon entries are capped daily; book Big Lagoon slots early through your tour operator.
Bring dry bags, reef safe sunscreen and water shoes for sharp rocks.

places.name: Coron
places.line: Volcanic lakes, sunken Japanese wrecks and jagged limestone islands.
places.about: Coron Island, across the water from Coron town on Busuanga, is ancestral land of the Tagbanua people, who run its lakes and lagoons. Below the surface, Second World War shipwrecks make it one of the best wreck diving spots anywhere.
tips: Each site on Coron Island charges its own entry fee, set by the Tagbanua; tours may or may not include them.
Kayangan Lake has a steep stair climb, so bring water.
Climb Mount Tapyas in town for sunset, then soak at Maquinit Hot Spring.

places.name: Puerto Princesa Underground River
places.line: Paddle into a vast cave where a river flows straight to the sea.
places.about: The Puerto Princesa Subterranean River runs for over 8 km under a limestone mountain, and the tour paddles about 1.5 km in. It is a World Heritage site and one of the New 7 Wonders of Nature, reached by boat from Sabang.
tips: You need a visitor permit; daily numbers are capped, so book 3 to 5 days ahead at the City Coliseum office or through your hotel.
Bring your passport and permit to Sabang wharf.
Keep your mouth closed when looking up: there are bats, and plenty of droppings.

places.line: A quiet bay village between Puerto Princesa and El Nido.
places.about: Port Barton is a sleepy fishing village on a bay full of small islands and reefs. It has little nightlife and spotty power, which is the point: hammocks, turtles and island hopping without the El Nido crowds.
tips: Bring enough cash: ATMs are few and often empty.
Power and wifi can be limited; download maps and books before you arrive.
Join a shared island hopping trip for turtles at Turtle Spot and German Island.

places.name: Cebu City heritage
places.line: Where Spanish rule in the Philippines began, in 1521.
places.about: The oldest city in the country keeps Magellan's Cross, the Basilica of the Santo Niño and the small Fort San Pedro close together. Around them are old houses, busy markets and a great food scene.
tips: The three main sights are a 10 minute walk apart; see them in one morning.
Dress modestly for the basilica, and mind your bag in the crowds around it.
The third week of January is Sinulog, the city's huge festival: book far ahead.

places.name: Kawasan Falls
places.line: Milky blue waterfalls at the end of a canyoneering adventure.
places.about: Kawasan's turquoise pools sit in a jungle gorge in Badian, an hour south of Moalboal. Most people get there by canyoneering: jumping, sliding and swimming down the Kanlaob river with a guide.
tips: Book canyoneering with an accredited operator; helmets and life jackets are a must.
Jumps are optional; tell your guide if you want to skip one.
Wear shoes that grip and can get wet, and leave valuables at your hotel.

places.name: Moalboal sardine run
places.line: Millions of sardines swirling just off the beach.
places.about: A huge school of sardines lives off Panagsama Beach all year, moving like a single dark cloud a few metres from the reef wall. Sea turtles feed nearby, and Pescador Island offers great diving.
tips: Swim out from Panagsama with a mask and fins; the sardines are just past the reef edge.
Take a guide if you are not a strong swimmer: currents can pick up.
Do not touch the turtles or stand on the coral.

places.name: Malapascua
places.line: A small island famous for dawn dives with thresher sharks.
places.about: Malapascua is a small, quiet island off the north tip of Cebu. Divers come for thresher sharks, seen most mornings at Monad Shoal, and everyone else for white sand, no cars and slow days.
tips: Thresher dives leave about 4:30 to 5 am; book the day before.
You need some diving experience for Monad Shoal; ask about the advanced course.
Bring cash: card payments and ATMs are limited.

places.name: Bantayan Island
places.line: Flat, quiet island with fine white beaches and fresh seafood.
places.about: Bantayan is a low island off north Cebu, with soft white sand at Santa Fe and Paradise Beach and calm, shallow water. It is laid back, cheap and best explored by scooter.
tips: Rent a scooter or tricycle to see the island; it is flat and the roads are quiet.
Try the dried fish (danggit) and fresh seafood in Bantayan town.
Holy Week is extremely busy; the island has special rules on eating meat then.

places.name: Chocolate Hills
places.line: Over 1,200 grassy hills that turn brown in the dry season.
places.about: Bohol's Chocolate Hills are a strange field of round, even hills that look like chocolate drops when the grass dries. The main viewpoint in Carmen sits on a hill above them.
tips: Go in the dry months (March to May) for the brown chocolate colour; they are green in the rains.
Combine it with the Tarsier Sanctuary and the Loboc river cruise on a countryside tour.
Avoid private tarsier 'zoos'; use the Philippine Tarsier Foundation sanctuary in Corella.

places.name: Panglao
places.line: Bohol's beach island, with dive reefs and dolphin trips.
places.about: Panglao is joined to Bohol by bridges and holds Alona Beach, Bohol's tourism hub. Boats leave at dawn for dolphins and the Balicasag reef, a top snorkelling and diving site.
tips: Leave by 6 am for dolphin watching off Pamilacan; that is when they are most active.
Alona Beach is busy; Dumaluan and Doljo are calmer.
Check your island hopping boat has life jackets for everyone.

places.name: Siquijor
places.line: A small mystical island with waterfalls, old churches and sunsets.
places.about: Siquijor has a reputation for healers and folk magic, but visitors find a friendly, quiet island with clear water, a ring road and waterfalls. It is easy to circle by scooter in a day.
tips: Rent a scooter and ride the 72 km ring road in a day.
Visit Cambugahay Falls early, before the tour groups.
Keep pesos ready for the island's ecological fee when you leave.

places.name: Apo Island
places.line: A tiny island with a famous marine sanctuary and many turtles.
places.about: Apo Island is a community run marine sanctuary off Negros, and one of the best known reefs in the country. Sea turtles feed near the beach, and the coral is bright and healthy.
tips: Leave from Malatapay (Zamboanguita) early to get calm water and fewer boats.
Snorkel only with a local guide; they keep you in the right zones.
Do not touch or chase turtles; keep a few metres away.

places.name: Boracay
places.line: A 4 km stretch of powder white sand and famous sunsets.
places.about: Boracay's White Beach is one of the best known beaches in Asia, with soft sand, calm water in the dry months and lively bars. After a big clean up in 2018 there are firm rules: no smoking or drinking on the beach, and capped visitor numbers.
tips: Arrive with your hotel booking: it is checked at the Caticlan jetty.
Pay the environmental and terminal fees at Caticlan; keep the receipts.
In the wet season (June to October) the wind turns and White Beach gets seaweed and waves; Bulabog becomes the calm side.

places.name: Iloilo City and the Miagao church
places.line: A gracious old sugar city and a World Heritage church nearby.
places.about: Iloilo City has some of the finest old houses and churches in the country, a riverside esplanade and famous food. An hour west, the Miagao Church is a World Heritage baroque church with a carved façade.
tips: Take a jeepney or bus from Iloilo to Miagao; it takes about an hour.
Try La Paz batchoy where it was invented.
The Dinagyang festival is held in late January; book ahead.

places.name: Guimaras

places.about: Guimaras sits just off Iloilo City and is known for mangoes said to be among the sweetest in the world. It has quiet beaches, islets, a Trappist monastery and roads perfect for cycling.
tips: Take the 15 minute boat from Ortiz or Parola wharf in Iloilo to Jordan.
Hire a tricycle for the day to see the main stops.

places.name: Siargao

places.about: Siargao is best known for Cloud 9, a heavy reef break, but the island is now a laid back hub for surfers and beach lovers. Coconut palms, rock pools and lagoons fill a slow, friendly island.

places.name: Camiguin

places.name: Davao City
places.line: A clean, green and well run city at the foot of Mount Apo.
places.about: Davao is Mindanao's biggest city and known for its strict rules, good food and fruit. Durian, the city's pride, is sold everywhere, and Samal Island's beaches are a short ferry away.
tips: Smoking, loud noise and fireworks are tightly banned; follow local rules.
Taste durian at the Magsaysay fruit stands; it is not allowed in many hotels.
Check current travel advice for Mindanao; Davao City itself is popular with visitors.

cities.name: Manila
cities.getAround: Grab cars across the city usually cost 150 to 500 pesos, more in rain or rush hour. The LRT and MRT cost about 15 to 35 pesos a ride; a Beep card saves queuing. Jeepneys start at about 13 to 15 pesos. White metered taxis are fine if the meter runs.
cities.stayArea: Stay in Makati (Poblacion or Legazpi Village) or BGC for food, nightlife and easy Grab rides; Ermita and Malate are cheaper and closer to Intramuros.

timing.avoid: Jul to Oct: typhoon season, heavy rain and street flooding.
timing.note: Christmas season starts in September and malls get packed; Holy Week empties the city as everyone heads home.

vibe.line: Huge, hot and chaotic, with old Spanish walls, the oldest Chinatown in the world and rooftop bars.

eat.name: Dong Bei Dumplings, Binondo
eat.what: Hand-made pork and chive dumplings in a tiny shop; a Binondo food crawl favourite.

eat.name: Salcedo Saturday Market, Makati
eat.what: Weekend morning market: grilled meats, regional dishes, fresh fruit and coffee.

eat.name: Aristocrat, Roxas Boulevard
eat.what: Old-school Filipino diner famous for chicken barbecue with java rice.

do.name: Intramuros walking loop
do.what: The old walled city: Fort Santiago, San Agustin Church and cobbled streets. Rent a bamboo bike or just walk.

do.name: National Museum of Fine Arts
do.what: Free national collection including Juan Luna's giant Spoliarium.

do.name: Rizal Park and Manila Bay sunset
do.what: Big city park next to the bay; the sunset over the water is the free show.

night.name: Poblacion, Makati
night.what: Party: small bars, rooftop spots, speakeasies and street food packed into a few blocks.

night.name: Bonifacio High Street, BGC
night.what: Chill: open-air street of bars and restaurants, safe and walkable late.

night.name: Remedios Circle, Malate
night.what: Old-school nightlife pocket with cheap beer, live music and karaoke.

know: Allow at least 2 hours to reach NAIA at rush hour; Manila traffic is among the worst in Asia.
A friendly stranger who invites you home or to a party, or asks for help with a sick relative, can be a drink-spiking scam. Politely say no.
At NAIA, use Grab or the official airport taxi queues and ignore touts in the arrivals hall.

cities.name: Baguio
cities.getAround: Metered taxis are cheap: most rides in town cost 80 to 200 pesos. Jeepneys cost about 13 to 15 pesos. The centre around Session Road is walkable but hilly.
cities.stayArea: Stay near Session Road and Burnham Park, so you can walk to the market, cafés and the bus terminals.

timing.avoid: Jul to Sep: typhoons and landslides on the mountain roads.
timing.note: Panagbenga flower festival in February brings parades and heavy traffic; Christmas and Holy Week weekends are packed.

vibe.line: The pine-scented summer capital: cool nights, strawberries, art and busy weekend crowds.

eat.name: Good Shepherd Convent
eat.what: Nuns' shop selling ube jam, peanut brittle and cookies; queue early on weekends.

eat.name: Café by the Ruins
eat.what: Arty garden café with Cordillera dishes, rice coffee and fresh bread.

eat.name: Baguio Public Market
eat.what: Strawberries, highland vegetables, local coffee and cheap carinderia meals.

do.name: Burnham Park boats
do.what: Row a boat or rent a bike around the lake in the park at the centre of town.

do.name: BenCab Museum
do.what: Top Filipino artist's museum with Cordillera art and a garden café.

do.name: La Trinidad strawberry farm
do.what: Pick your own strawberries just outside the city, best Dec to Apr.

night.name: Harrison Road night market
night.what: Street stalls with fried snacks, ukay-ukay clothes and grilled skewers.

night.name: Session Road cafés and bars
night.what: Chill: acoustic live music, local craft beer and hot drinks on cold nights.

night.name: Ili-Likha Artists Village
night.what: Arty: quirky multi-level art space with small food stalls and cafés.

know: Nights drop to about 12 to 15 C from December to February; bring a warm layer.
Weekends and long holidays fill the city with Manila visitors; book rooms ahead and travel midweek if you can.
Buy return bus tickets early for Sunday afternoons; buses back to Manila sell out.

cities.name: Banaue
cities.getAround: Tricycles cost about 50 to 150 pesos for short hops. A tricycle to the Batad saddle and back is roughly 1,000 to 1,500 pesos per vehicle. From the saddle you walk down to Batad village.
cities.stayArea: Stay in the town centre near the market and the jeepney stop, or spend a night in a homestay in Batad right above the terraces.

timing.avoid: Jul to Oct: rain, slippery trails and landslides on the Bontoc road.
timing.note: The terraces are greenest from about April to July and silver with water around January to February; harvest is roughly June to July.

vibe.line: Mountain villages and 2,000-year-old rice terraces carved by hand into the Cordillera.

eat.name: Town-centre carinderias
eat.what: Rice, vegetables and stews in simple canteens by the market.

eat.name: Lodge restaurants with terrace views
eat.what: Pinikpikan chicken soup and highland rice in the inns above town.

eat.name: Batad homestay kitchens
eat.what: Simple meals with mountain rice and coffee, looking over the amphitheatre terraces.

do.name: Banaue viewpoint
do.what: The classic photo spot over the terraces, a short tricycle ride from town.

do.name: Batad and Tappiya Falls hike
do.what: Walk down through the amphitheatre terraces to a big waterfall; hire a local guide.

do.name: Bangaan village
do.what: A small traditional village set in its own terraces, a quieter alternative to Batad.

night.name: Lodge rice wine
night.what: Chill: try tapuy, local rice wine, by the fire at your inn.

night.name: Stargazing in Batad
night.what: Quiet: no road and little light, so the sky is huge on clear nights.

night.name: Early night, early hike
night.what: Quiet: town goes to bed by 9 pm; trails are best in the cool morning.

know: Bring enough cash: ATMs are few and often empty or offline.
Hire guides through the tourism office in Banaue or Batad; rates are fixed and posted.
An environmental fee is collected at the Batad saddle; keep the receipt.

cities.name: Sagada
cities.getAround: The village is small enough to walk. Tour vans and jeeps take you to far viewpoints. Every visitor registers and pays a fee at the tourism office, which also books the cave and trail guides.
cities.stayArea: Stay along the main road near the tourism office and the town hall, an easy walk to the caves, cafés and Echo Valley.

timing.avoid: Jul to Sep: heavy rain, foggy roads and closed caves.
timing.note: Sunrise over the sea of clouds at Kiltepan is best on cold, clear mornings in December to February.

vibe.line: Pine forests, hanging coffins and lemon pie in a cool mountain village.

eat.name: Yoghurt House
eat.what: Homemade yoghurt with granola and fruit, plus hearty mountain meals.

eat.name: Sagada Lemon Pie House
eat.what: Famous lemon and egg pies; buy a box for the bus.

eat.name: Gaia Café
eat.what: Vegetarian café in the pines with views over the rice fields.

do.name: Echo Valley and hanging coffins
do.what: Short guided walk to coffins hung on the cliff face, a local burial tradition.

do.name: Sumaguing Cave
do.what: Guided cave walk with rock formations and cold pools; wear shoes that can get wet.

do.name: Kiltepan sunrise
do.what: Pre-dawn ride to watch the clouds fill the valleys below the peaks.

night.name: Log Cabin dinner
night.what: Cosy wood-panelled restaurant with good set dinners; book ahead.

night.name: Inn bonfire
night.what: Chill: hot drinks and a fire at your guesthouse on cold nights.

night.name: Stargazing on the main road
night.what: Quiet: clear mountain skies when the fog lifts.

know: Sagada has a 9 pm curfew for noise and drinking in public; respect it.
Caves and the hanging coffins must be visited with a registered guide from the tourism office.
The coffins are graves, not props: do not touch them or climb on them.

cities.name: Vigan
cities.getAround: The old town is best on foot. Tricycles cost about 20 to 50 pesos around town. Kalesa horse carts charge a set hourly rate; ask to see the city rate card first.
cities.stayArea: Stay in a restored heritage house in the old town near Calle Crisologo, so you can see the street lit up at night.

timing.avoid: Jul to Sep: typhoons and heavy rain on the Ilocos coast.
timing.note: Vigan Longganisa Festival is in late January; Holy Week brings big crowds.

vibe.line: Cobbled lanes and Spanish-era mansions, with empanada stalls on every square.

eat.name: Plaza Burgos empanada stalls
eat.what: Crispy orange empanada with egg, longganisa and green papaya, fried to order.

eat.name: Café Leona, Calle Crisologo
eat.what: Ilocano dishes like bagnet and pinakbet at the head of the heritage street.

eat.name: Hidden Garden
eat.what: Garden restaurant on the edge of town with Ilocano food and native snacks.

do.name: Calle Crisologo walk
do.what: The famous cobbled street of old mansions; go early morning to skip the crowds.

do.name: Bantay Bell Tower
do.what: Old brick watchtower on a hill with views over the town.

do.name: Pagburnayan pottery
do.what: Watch potters make burnay clay jars by hand, the old way.

night.name: Plaza Salcedo dancing fountain
night.what: Free evening light and water show by the cathedral.

night.name: Calle Crisologo by lamplight
night.what: Quiet: the heritage street lit by old-style lamps after dark.

night.name: Plaza Burgos night snacks
night.what: Food: empanada, okoy and halo-halo stalls stay busy into the evening.

know: Kalesa drivers charge per hour; the city posts official rates, so ask to see them.
Laoag airport is about 80 km away, so a flight plus van often takes as long as the night bus.
Buy Vigan longganisa and bagnet in the market for gifts; they keep for a few days.

cities.name: San Juan, La Union
cities.getAround: Jeepneys and buses run along the coast road for about 13 to 30 pesos. Tricycles do short rides for 20 to 100 pesos. Scooter rental is about 400 to 600 pesos a day.
cities.stayArea: Stay along the Urbiztondo strip in San Juan, in walking distance of the surf breaks and beach bars.

timing.avoid: Jul to Sep: typhoons, big messy waves and rain.
timing.note: The best surf for beginners runs from about October to March; weekends fill up with Manila crowds.

vibe.line: Easy beginner surf, cafés and sunset bars a few hours north of Manila.

eat.name: El Union Coffee
eat.what: Surf-town café with good coffee and shakes right on the strip.

eat.name: Halo-Halo de Iloko
eat.what: Big bowls of halo-halo and Ilocano snacks in a colourful native-style house.

eat.name: Gefseis Greek Grill
eat.what: Homestyle Greek food that surfers queue for.

do.name: Surf lesson at Urbiztondo
do.what: An hour with a local instructor including the board.

do.name: Tangadan Falls
do.what: Jungle river hike to a big waterfall in San Gabriel; local guide required.

do.name: Ma-Cho Temple
do.what: Colourful Taoist temple on a hill above San Fernando with sea views.

night.name: Flotsam and Jetsam
night.what: Party: beachfront hostel bar with bonfires, DJs and a young surfer crowd.

night.name: Urbiztondo sunset bars
night.what: Chill: beanbags and beer on the sand as the sun drops into the sea.

night.name: Live acoustic on the strip
night.what: Chill: small bars along the main road with local bands on weekends.

know: Rip currents can be strong; swim near surfers and lifeguards, not alone on empty stretches.
Weekend prices jump and rooms sell out with Manila visitors; come midweek for calm and better rates.
Buses to Manila from the highway fill on Sunday afternoons; book or leave early.

cities.name: Tagaytay
cities.getAround: Jeepneys run along the ridge road for about 13 to 30 pesos. Tricycles charge 50 to 150 pesos for short hops. Grab cars are limited, so a hired car is easier for day trips.
cities.stayArea: Stay on the ridge road between Sky Ranch and Picnic Grove for views over Taal Lake.

timing.avoid: Jul to Oct: rain and fog hide the volcano.
timing.note: Weekend traffic from Manila is heavy; come on a weekday morning for clear views.

vibe.line: Cool ridge-top town with bulalo soup and big views over the Taal volcano lake.

eat.name: Mahogany Market bulalo
eat.what: Beef shank and bone-marrow soup in no-frills stalls; share one pot.

eat.name: Bag of Beans
eat.what: Garden café with pies, breakfast and coffee in the cool air.

eat.name: Sonya's Garden
eat.what: Set lunch of salad, pasta and bread in a flower garden.

do.name: Picnic Grove
do.what: Park on the ridge with the best wide view of Taal Lake and the volcano.

do.name: Sky Ranch
do.what: Small amusement park with a big Ferris wheel over the lake.

do.name: Taal Volcano boat trip from Talisay
do.what: Boat across the lake to the volcano island when alert levels allow.

night.name: Ridge cafés with a view
night.what: Chill: hot chocolate and cake with the lights of the lake below.

night.name: Sky Ranch at night
night.what: Fun: rides and the lit-up Ferris wheel in the cool evening.

night.name: Late bulalo dinner
night.what: Food: Mahogany Market stalls stay open late for hot soup.

know: Access to the volcano island depends on the Phivolcs alert level; check before you book a boat.
Avoid Saturday and Sunday afternoons: the ridge road jams with day-trippers.
Bring a light jacket; evenings are noticeably cooler than Manila.

cities.name: Puerto Galera
cities.getAround: Shared jeepneys link Sabang, the town and White Beach for about 30 to 80 pesos. Tricycles and motorbike taxis do short trips. Boats between beaches can be hired by the hour.
cities.stayArea: Stay in Sabang for diving and nightlife, White Beach for families and budget rooms, or Big La Laguna for something quieter.

timing.avoid: Jul to Sep: rough seas and typhoons can cancel ferries.
timing.note: Holy Week is wild and fully booked; diving is good year round.

vibe.line: A short hop from Manila for coral reefs, dive shops and a lively beach strip.

eat.name: Sabang beachfront grills
eat.what: Grilled fish, squid and pork skewers along the dive beach.

eat.name: White Beach food stalls
eat.what: Cheap Filipino meals and fruit shakes near the busy sand.

eat.name: Badladz, Sabang
eat.what: Long-running bar and restaurant with Mexican dishes and sea views.

do.name: Fun dive at Sabang
do.what: Close, colourful reefs and wrecks; many shops along the beach.

do.name: Tamaraw Falls
do.what: Roadside waterfall on the way to Calapan with a cool pool.

do.name: Snorkelling at Small La Laguna
do.what: Calm water and coral right off the beach.

night.name: Sabang bar strip
night.what: Party: dive bars and late beer by the water.

night.name: White Beach fire dancers
night.what: Fun: fire shows, beach bars and the local Mindoro Sling cocktail.

night.name: Sunset drinks at Big La Laguna
night.what: Chill: quieter beach bars with sunset views.

know: An environmental fee and a terminal fee are charged at the port on arrival; keep the receipts.
Last boats back to Batangas leave in the afternoon; check the time on arrival.
Holy Week and long weekends sell out weeks ahead.

cities.name: Legazpi
cities.getAround: Jeepneys cost about 13 to 15 pesos and tricycles 20 to 60 pesos around town. Grab is limited. Hire a van or join an ATV tour for the Mayon side of town.
cities.stayArea: Stay in the city centre near Peñaranda Park, close to the Grand Central Terminal for vans to Donsol.

timing.avoid: Sep to Dec: Bicol's peak typhoon months.
timing.note: Mayon is often hidden by cloud by mid-morning; go early. Trails close when the alert level rises.

vibe.line: A city at the foot of a near-perfect volcano, famous for spicy coconut cooking.

eat.name: 1st Colonial Grill
eat.what: Bicol Express, pinangat and chilli ice cream.

eat.name: Small Talk Café
eat.what: Local favourites like pasta with pinangat and Bicol dishes.

eat.name: Legazpi Boulevard stalls
eat.what: Grilled snacks and fishball carts along the seafront walk.

do.name: Cagsawa Ruins
do.what: Bell tower of a church buried by Mayon in 1814, with the volcano behind.

do.name: Mayon ATV tour
do.what: Ride over old lava fields towards the volcano.

do.name: Ligñon Hill
do.what: Short climb or drive to a viewpoint over the city and Mayon.

night.name: Legazpi Boulevard
night.what: Chill: seafront walk and jogging path, busy at sunset.

night.name: Embarcadero de Legazpi
night.what: Easy: waterfront mall with restaurants and bay views.

night.name: Videoke bars in town
night.what: Local fun: karaoke and cold beer with Bicolano crowds.

know: Mayon's alert level changes; check Phivolcs before booking hikes or ATV tours.
Bicol food is hot: ask for less chilli if you need to.
Vans to Donsol leave from the Grand Central Terminal when full, so go in the morning.

cities.name: Donsol
cities.getAround: A small town: tricycles cost about 20 to 150 pesos, including the run out to the visitor centre at Dancalan.
cities.stayArea: Stay on the road between the town and the Butanding Visitor Centre at Dancalan, where the resorts face the sea.

timing.avoid: Jun to Nov: whale sharks are mostly gone and rain is heavier.
timing.note: The whale shark season runs roughly December to May; sightings are never guaranteed.

vibe.line: A sleepy fishing town where you snorkel next to whale sharks.

eat.name: Town market eateries
eat.what: Simple Bicolano meals: laing, pinangat and grilled fish.

eat.name: Dancalan resort restaurants
eat.what: Seafood and Filipino dishes facing the beach.

eat.name: Roadside barbecue stands
eat.what: Pork and chicken skewers grilled in the evening.

do.name: Whale shark interaction
do.what: Register at the visitor centre, then share a boat with a spotter and a guide.

do.name: Ogod River firefly cruise
do.what: Paddle boat at dusk to see trees lit up by fireflies.

do.name: Manta Bowl dive trip
do.what: Deep-water day trip to see manta rays in the Ticao Pass.

night.name: Firefly river cruise
night.what: Quiet: the best Donsol night out, on a slow boat in the dark.

night.name: Beach bonfires at the resorts
night.what: Chill: beers on the sand after a day at sea.

night.name: Videoke in town
night.what: Local fun: karaoke bars along the main road.

know: No touching, no flash and stay at least a few metres from the sharks; guides enforce it.
Bring cash: there are few ATMs and they can run dry in peak weeks.
Boats go out in the morning; arrive the evening before to be first in line.

cities.name: Puerto Princesa
cities.getAround: Tricycles are everywhere and cost about 15 to 60 pesos around the city; there is no Grab. Vans to Sabang, Port Barton and El Nido leave from the San Jose terminal or pick up from hotels.
cities.stayArea: Stay along Rizal Avenue between the airport and the Baywalk, close to restaurants and tour pick-ups.

timing.avoid: Jul to Oct: rough seas can cancel the Underground River boats.
timing.note: Underground River permits are limited each day; book a few days ahead in peak season.

vibe.line: Palawan's clean, easygoing capital and the jump-off for the Underground River.

eat.name: Kalui Restaurant
eat.what: Seafood set meals in a wooden house; shoes off at the door, book ahead.

eat.name: Baywalk grilled seafood
eat.what: Pick fish and squid and have it grilled by the bay.

eat.name: Kinabuchs Grill and Bar
eat.what: Try tamilok, the local woodworm, plus grilled food and cold beer.

do.name: Honda Bay island hopping
do.what: Day of beaches and snorkelling on small islands near the city.

do.name: Plaza Cuartel
do.what: Small war memorial park with a sad wartime story.

do.name: Iwahig firefly watching
do.what: Night paddle on the Iwahig River among fireflies.

night.name: Baywalk night stalls
night.what: Chill: families, food carts and a cool breeze by the water.

night.name: Kinabuchs
night.what: Social: the city's busiest open-air bar on Rizal Avenue.

night.name: Iwahig River firefly cruise
night.what: Quiet: mangroves lit by fireflies on a moonless night.

know: The Underground River needs a permit with a fixed daily number; book through a tour or the city office in advance.
Tricycle fares have a fixed minimum in the city; agree the price first for longer trips.
Vans to El Nido fill fast in the morning; reserve a seat the day before.

cities.name: El Nido
cities.getAround: Tricycles cost about 50 to 250 pesos from town to Corong Corong or Lio, and roughly 1,200 to 1,800 pesos per trike for a Nacpan round trip. Scooters rent for about 500 to 700 pesos a day.
cities.stayArea: Stay in El Nido town for budget rooms and tour pick-ups, Corong Corong for sunsets, or Lio for a quieter beach near the airport.

timing.avoid: Jul to Oct: southwest monsoon, choppy seas and cancelled tours.
timing.note: The Small and Big Lagoons have daily slots; book Tour A early in peak season.

vibe.line: Limestone cliffs, hidden lagoons and island-hopping boats every morning.

eat.name: Artcafé
eat.what: Big menu, good breakfasts and a tour desk in the town centre.

eat.name: Trattoria Altrove
eat.what: Wood-fired pizza in town; expect a queue at dinner.

eat.name: Corong Corong food stalls
eat.what: Cheap grilled food and rice meals along the road.

do.name: Island hopping Tour A
do.what: Bacuit Bay lagoons, beaches and snorkel stops, lunch on board.

do.name: Nacpan Beach
do.what: Long golden beach about an hour north of town, quiet and wide.

do.name: Taraw Cliff via ferrata
do.what: Guided climb up the cliff behind town for a view over the bay.

night.name: Pukka Bar
night.what: Party: reggae and live music on the beach in town.

night.name: Las Cabanas sunset
night.what: Chill: beach bars with the best sunset, a short ride south.

night.name: Lio Beach evening
night.what: Quiet: a calm walk and dinner on the newer beach strip.

know: Everyone pays the Eco-Tourism Development Fee before island hopping; keep the card for every tour.
ATMs can run out of cash; bring enough pesos from Puerto Princesa or Manila.
Power and water cuts happen; pick a room with a generator if it matters to you.

cities.name: Coron
cities.getAround: Tricycles cost about 30 to 100 pesos in town. Shared vans from Busuanga airport cost about 150 to 250 pesos and take 40 minutes. Scooters rent for 500 to 700 pesos a day.
cities.stayArea: Stay in Coron town near the public market and the foot of Mt Tapyas, where tours and dive shops pick up.

timing.avoid: Jul to Oct: rough seas, typhoons and cancelled tours.
timing.note: Kayangan Lake and Twin Lagoon are busiest late morning; ask for an early boat.

vibe.line: Clear lakes, limestone islands and Japanese wartime wrecks under the sea.

eat.name: Coron public market paluto
eat.what: Buy fresh seafood and have it cooked next door.

eat.name: Kawayanan Grill
eat.what: Bamboo-hut restaurant with grilled seafood and local dishes.

eat.name: Town carinderias
eat.what: Cheap rice meals and pancit around the plaza.

do.name: Coron Island tour
do.what: Kayangan Lake, Twin Lagoon and beaches; entry fees often extra.

do.name: Mt Tapyas
do.what: About 700 steps up to a big cross and a sunset view.

do.name: Wreck diving
do.what: World-famous WWII wrecks; two dives with gear.

night.name: Maquinit Hot Spring
night.what: Relax: saltwater hot spring by the mangroves, lovely after dark.

night.name: Mt Tapyas sunset
night.what: Chill: watch the sun drop over the islands from the top.

night.name: Town bars on the main road
night.what: Social: dive-crowd bars with cheap beer.

know: Kayangan Lake and other sites are run by the Tagbanua people and charge their own entrance fees.
Busuanga airport is about 40 minutes from town; book the shared van with your hotel.
Book wreck dives a day ahead; the best sites need a full day out.

cities.name: Port Barton
cities.getAround: The village is tiny: you walk everywhere. Boats take you to nearby beaches and islands for set prices posted at the tourism desk.
cities.stayArea: Stay on the main beach for cafés and boats, or on White Beach next door for something quieter.

timing.avoid: Jul to Oct: rough seas and fewer boats.
timing.note: A good slow stop between Puerto Princesa and El Nido, with far fewer crowds.

vibe.line: A laid-back fishing village with starfish sandbars and no traffic.

eat.name: Jambalaya Cajun Café
eat.what: Cajun dishes and fresh fish on the main beach.

eat.name: Village carinderias
eat.what: Rice, fish and vegetables for very little.

eat.name: Beachfront grills
eat.what: The day's catch, grilled in the evening.

do.name: Island hopping tour
do.what: Starfish sandbar, turtles, coral gardens and a beach lunch.

do.name: Pamuayan Falls
do.what: Short jungle walk to a small waterfall and pool.

do.name: White Beach walk
do.what: Easy coastal walk to the next bay.

night.name: Beach bonfires
night.what: Chill: guesthouses light fires on the sand.

night.name: Barefoot beach bars
night.what: Social: a few bars with live acoustic music.

night.name: Stargazing
night.what: Quiet: little light here, so the sky is clear and full.

know: There is no reliable ATM: bring all the cash you need.
Power cuts are common; bring a power bank.
Book the van out a day ahead; seats to El Nido and Puerto Princesa fill fast.

cities.name: Cebu City
cities.getAround: Grab cars cost about 100 to 350 pesos across the city. Metered taxis are fine. Jeepneys start at about 13 to 15 pesos. Ceres buses leave from the South Bus Terminal (Moalboal, Oslob) and the North Bus Terminal (Maya, Hagnaya).
cities.stayArea: Stay near IT Park or Lahug for food and safe late nights, Fuente Osmeña for budget rooms, or Mactan for beach resorts by the airport.

timing.avoid: Aug to Nov: typhoon risk and heavy rain.
timing.note: Sinulog in mid January is the biggest party of the year; book rooms months ahead.

vibe.line: The oldest Spanish city in the country and the gateway to the Visayas islands.

eat.name: Rico's Lechon
eat.what: Crispy roast pig, plain or spicy, the Cebu way.

eat.name: Larsian BBQ
eat.what: Open-air barbecue stalls with hanging rice and cheap skewers.

eat.name: Sutukil on Mactan
eat.what: Pick fresh seafood and have it grilled, stewed or raw in vinegar.

do.name: Magellan's Cross and Santo Niño Basilica
do.what: The cross from 1521 and the city's most loved church.

do.name: Fort San Pedro
do.what: Small Spanish fort near the port.

do.name: Temple of Leah
do.what: Grand Roman-style temple in the hills with city views.

night.name: Sugbo Mercado, IT Park
night.what: Food: weekend night market with dozens of stalls.

night.name: IT Park bars
night.what: Party: bars and clubs open late in the business district.

night.name: Tops Lookout
night.what: Views: city lights from the hills at night.

know: Cebu has two big bus terminals: South for Moalboal and Oslob, North for Maya and Hagnaya.
Pier 1 and the other piers are separate; check which pier your ferry uses.
Sinulog in January brings huge crowds; expect road closures and surge prices.

cities.name: Moalboal
cities.getAround: A tricycle from the highway to Panagsama Beach costs about 100 to 150 pesos. Habal-habal motorbike taxis are cheaper. Scooters rent for about 350 to 500 pesos a day.
cities.stayArea: Stay on Panagsama Beach for the sardines and dive shops, or White Beach (Basdaku) for sand and calm water.

timing.avoid: Aug to Nov: rain and typhoon risk.
timing.note: The sardine run is there all year, but go early before the boats.

vibe.line: Swim with millions of sardines off the beach, then go canyoneering in turquoise rivers.

eat.name: Lantaw Native Restaurant
eat.what: Filipino and seafood dishes on a deck over the water.

eat.name: Panagsama carinderias
eat.what: Cheap rice meals for divers on a budget.

eat.name: Shaka Moalboal
eat.what: Smoothie bowls and healthy plates near the beach.

do.name: Sardine run snorkel
do.what: Swim from the shore into a giant sardine ball, often with turtles.

do.name: Pescador Island
do.what: Boat trip to a small island with steep coral walls.

do.name: Kawasan Falls canyoneering
do.what: Jump, slide and swim down the river to the falls with a guide.

night.name: Chili Bar
night.what: Party: long-running beach bar, pool tables and late drinks.

night.name: Panagsama sunset bars
night.what: Chill: drinks on the seawall as the sun drops.

night.name: Dive-shop evening talks
night.what: Social: logbook beers with other divers.

events.name: Feast of the Immaculate Conception
events.what: Special non-working day: Catholic feast with packed churches and town processions.
events.tip: Banks and offices close; malls stay open and get busy.

events.name: Christmas light shows in Makati
events.what: Ayala Triangle Gardens turns into a free light and music show every evening of the season.
events.tip: Shows run every 30 minutes or so after dark; come on a weekday to avoid the crush.

events.name: Simbang Gabi (dawn Christmas masses)
events.what: Nine dawn or evening masses before Christmas, with bibingka and puto bumbong sold outside every church.
events.tip: The dates are fixed by tradition; go early for a seat and stay for the rice cakes afterwards.

events.name: Giant Lantern Festival, San Fernando (Pampanga)
events.what: Barangays compete with huge spinning lanterns lit by thousands of bulbs, then display them until New Year.
events.tip: San Fernando is about 1.5 to 2 hours north of Manila by bus; the contest night is the big one, so book a ride back.

events.name: Christmas Eve
events.what: Special non-working day. Families gather for midnight mass and the Noche Buena feast.
events.tip: Shops close early; buses and ferries out of Manila are full for days before.

events.name: Christmas Day
events.what: Regular holiday and the biggest day of the year: family lunches, open houses and carols.
events.tip: Many small eateries close; malls and hotel restaurants stay open.

events.name: Rizal Day
events.what: Regular holiday for national hero Jose Rizal, with a wreath ceremony at Rizal Park in Manila.
events.tip: Sits between Christmas and New Year, so expect a long holiday week and full resorts.

events.name: Last Day of the Year
events.what: Special non-working day before New Year's Eve: round fruits on the table and loud fireworks at midnight.
events.tip: Firecracker smoke is thick at midnight in cities; keep pets and kids indoors.

events.name: New Year's Eve countdowns in Manila
events.what: Free countdown concerts and fireworks around the Bay area, Bonifacio Global City and Eastwood.
events.tip: Roads close around the venues; take Grab early or stay within walking distance.

events.name: New Year's Eve on White Beach
events.what: Fireworks from resorts all along White Beach and beach bars open until dawn.
events.tip: Rooms sell out months ahead; Station 2 is loudest, Station 1 calmer.

events.name: New Year's Day
events.what: Regular holiday. Quiet morning after the midnight fireworks.
events.tip: Many shops open late or close; get cash before New Year's Eve.

events.name: Feast of the Black Nazarene (Traslacion)
events.what: Millions of barefoot devotees pull the Black Nazarene statue from Rizal Park to Quiapo Church, often for over 20 hours.
events.tip: Watch from a distance, keep valuables at the hotel and avoid the Quiapo area if you dislike crowds.

events.name: LaLaLa Fest Manila
events.what: One day festival at the Philippine Arena with Olivia Dean, BINI, Lola Amour, Up Dharma Down and more.
events.tip: The arena is in Bocaue, Bulacan, 1.5 to 3 hours from Manila in traffic; plan a shuttle or a shared car.

events.name: Vigan Longganisa Festival and City Fiesta
events.what: Vigan's fiesta for its garlicky sausage: street dancing, food fairs and the feast of Saint Paul on 25 January.
events.tip: Try longganisa with vinegar and garlic rice at the plaza stalls; rooms on Calle Crisologo fill up.

events.name: Sinulog
events.what: Cebu's huge Santo Nino festival: novena masses, a fluvial parade and the grand street dance parade on Sunday 17 January.
events.tip: Watching from the curb is free; book rooms months ahead and expect phone signal to drop in the crowds.

events.name: Ati-Atihan, Kalibo
events.what: Soot-painted dancers and drum groups fill Kalibo's streets; anyone can join the dancing.
events.tip: Kalibo is about 1.5 to 2 hours from the Caticlan jetty; wear clothes you don't mind getting painted.

events.name: La Union Longboard Classic (WSL Longboard Tour)
events.what: World Longboard Tour stop at Monaliza Point, Urbiztondo: the world's best loggers on a long right-hander.
events.tip: Free to watch from the beach; the contest runs on the best swell days inside the window.

events.name: Westlife 25th Anniversary Tour
events.what: The Irish band brings its anniversary tour to SM Mall of Asia Arena.
events.tip: Reports disagree on 20 or 27 January; check the ticket site before you book.

events.name: Dinagyang
events.what: Iloilo's Santo Nino festival with ten tribes dancing in the streets of the old city proper.
events.tip: Bring cash for street food along Calle Real; paid seats sell out, but standing is free.

events.name: KATSEYE in Manila

events.name: Easter Sunday

events.name: Day of Valour (Araw ng Kagitingan)

events.name: Ninoy Aquino Day

basics: Philippine peso (PHP). Cards work in malls, hotels and bigger restaurants; almost everything else is cash. Local ATMs charge foreign cards about 250 pesos per withdrawal, and many cap each withdrawal at 10,000 to 20,000 pesos. Carry enough cash before small islands, where ATMs are few and often empty.

Cheap domestic flights (Cebu Pacific, PAL, AirAsia) link the islands; ferries (2GO, OceanJet, Starlite) and outrigger bangkas cover shorter hops. In cities use Grab or metered taxis; in towns, tricycles and jeepneys. Vans and buses run between towns. Traffic in Manila is slow, so allow double the time.

Dry season is roughly December to May, hottest in April and May. The southwest monsoon brings rain from June to October to Manila, Luzon, Palawan and the western Visayas, and typhoons strike mostly from July to November, hardest in Luzon and the eastern Visayas. Siargao and the east coast are wetter from November to February. Mindanao sits mostly south of the typhoon belt. Baguio and Sagada get cold at night from December to February.

Filipinos are warm and indirect: smile, stay calm and never shout, because causing someone to lose face (hiya) goes badly. Add po for politeness, dress modestly in churches, and accept offered food with thanks. Toilets are called CR (comfort room). People often point with their lips and get your attention with a soft psst; it is not rude.

Drug laws are harsh and enforced. Smoking and vaping are banned in public places nationwide. Taking sand, shells or coral from beaches is illegal, and Boracay fines are steep. Don't photograph military or police sites, and respect liquor bans during elections and on some religious days.

Globe and Smart have counters at the main airports. Tourist SIMs must be registered with your passport and work for 30 days; an eSIM avoids the paperwork. Signal is patchy on small islands and in the mountains. Power is 220 V, 60 Hz, with type A, B and C sockets (flat US-style pins are common). Brownouts happen on smaller islands.

Register free on etravel.gov.ph within 72 hours before you arrive (and before you leave); use only the official site. Many nationalities get 30 days visa-free (Chinese and Indian visitors have shorter or different rules), with a passport valid at least 6 months and a return or onward ticket, which airlines check at check-in. Extensions are done at the Bureau of Immigration.

Call 911 for police, fire and ambulance anywhere. Philippine Red Cross: 143. Report lost passports to your embassy in Manila. Typhoon warnings come from PAGASA; the Coast Guard stops boats when a storm signal is raised.

wishIKnew.title: Terminal fees add up
wishIKnew.tip: Manila's international terminal fee (950 pesos) is usually in your ticket, but small airports and ports still want cash: Caticlan jetty 150 each way, Coron airport 100 when you fly out, plus small port fees elsewhere.

wishIKnew.title: Island environmental fees
wishIKnew.tip: Boracay charges foreigners 300 pesos (Filipinos 150), El Nido about 400 for its eco fee, Coron about 200 for 10 days. Pay cash, keep the receipt or wristband, you may be asked again.

wishIKnew.title: Grab beats the airport taxi
wishIKnew.tip: Grab works in Manila, Cebu, Davao, Iloilo and Baguio and shows the price up front. If you take a taxi, use the white metered ones and insist on the meter; the yellow airport taxis cost more.

wishIKnew.title: Agree the tricycle fare first
wishIKnew.tip: Shared tricycle hops in town cost about 15 to 50 pesos each; a private 'special trip' is 100 to 300. Settle the price before you sit down, and have small notes because drivers rarely have change.

wishIKnew.title: ATMs charge 250 a go
wishIKnew.tip: Most banks charge foreign cards about 250 pesos per withdrawal on top of your bank's fee, and limits can be 10,000 to 20,000 per try. Withdraw the maximum, decline the conversion, and keep a backup card.

wishIKnew.title: Bring cash to small islands
wishIKnew.tip: Siargao, El Nido, Siquijor, Camiguin, Malapascua and Port Barton have few ATMs and they run dry on weekends. Arrive with enough pesos for rooms, boats and food; many places don't take cards.

wishIKnew.title: Book ferries early in peak weeks
wishIKnew.tip: OceanJet, 2GO and Starlite sell online; at Christmas and Holy Week boats sell out days ahead. Arrive an hour early with your passport, and expect a small terminal fee on top of the fare.

wishIKnew.title: SIMs need your passport
wishIKnew.tip: Tourist SIMs are registered with your passport and run 30 days. Airport tourist bundles and the Globe or Smart tourist eSIMs (about 1,600 to 1,750 pesos) are pricier than normal prepaid promos from 99 pesos at any shop.

wishIKnew.title: Typhoons cancel boats fast
wishIKnew.tip: When a storm signal is raised the Coast Guard stops small boats, and flights to small islands cancel. From July to November, leave a spare day before any international flight home.

wishIKnew.title: Don't drink the tap water
wishIKnew.tip: Drink bottled or refilled water. Most hotels and hostels have refill stations, and water refilling shops in every town fill a bottle for a few pesos.

wishIKnew.title: San Miguel is cheap at the store
wishIKnew.tip: A bottle of San Miguel Pale Pilsen costs roughly 55 to 80 pesos at a sari-sari store or 7-Eleven, 80 to 150 in bars, and more on Boracay's beachfront. Red Horse is stronger than it tastes.

wishIKnew.title: Tipping is small and optional
wishIKnew.tip: Restaurants often add a 10% service charge; if not, leave small change. Round up for drivers, and give boat crews and guides about 50 to 100 pesos each after a good island hopping day.

wishIKnew.title: Island hopping tours are per person
wishIKnew.tip: Tours in El Nido, Coron and Siargao are sold per person and leave around 9 am; fees for lagoons and beaches are often extra. Ask what is included before you pay.

wishIKnew.title: Holy Week and Christmas change everything
wishIKnew.tip: During Holy Week and from mid-December to New Year, prices jump, transport sells out and Good Friday closes much of the country. Book early or travel just after.

pack: Passport (6+ months valid) and a photo of it
eTravel QR code from etravel.gov.ph, done within 72 hours of arrival
Proof of a return or onward ticket
Some pesos in small notes for arrival
One church outfit: shoulders and knees covered
A light jumper for cold buses, ferries and Baguio or Sagada nights
Sandals plus water shoes for boats, falls and coral
Insect repellent (dengue is common in the rainy season)
Rehydration salts and your usual medicines
Power bank for brownouts and long boat days
Plug adapter for type A, B and C sockets
Rain jacket or poncho (June to November)
